issues.failure_explanation: The abstract claims the SG uniqueness result is extended to p.c.f. fractals. The SG result (Theorem thm.main) includes uniqueness. Theorem thm.pcf only asserts existence of a HM satisfying the conditions, and the discussion explicitly states that uniqueness could not be claimed for general p.c.f. fractals. Thus the abstract materially overstates the established result.

issues.title: Abstract overclaims uniqueness for p.c.f. extension
issues.why_classification: The defect is a prose overclaim; correcting it is a local edit and does not alter any formal result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The key point is to check that $F$ is well defined as a continuous map from [0,1]\times G to \T

issues.failure_explanation: In $\T=\R/\Z$, scalar multiplication by $t\in(0,1)$ is not well-defined: changing a representative by an integer changes $t f(x)$ by a non-integer. Thus $F$ is not a well-defined map to $\T$. Even if interpreted via lifts on each loop, the proof only checks endpoint consistency along each $\gamma$ and does not verify consistency at points belonging to multiple loops. The converse implication is therefore not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the straight-line homotopy with a correct proof that equal degree vectors imply homotopic maps, e.g., by constructing a homotopy levelwise on the approximating graphs using lifts.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that the degree vector determines the homotopy class (Theorem thm.homotopy) is invalid; the claim remains unsupported by the given argument.
issues.title: Invalid straight-line homotopy in proof of thm.homotopy
issues.why_classification: The theorem statement is likely true, but the given proof's central construction is invalid; a new contained argument is needed to repair the proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The uniqueness of the minimizer \eqref{new-min} then implies

issues.failure_explanation: In the glued graph $\Gamma_m$, the vertex $z$ is identified as $z_+^{-r}\simeq z_-^0$. The proposed transformation assigns two different values to this same vertex: on the $V_m^0$ side it gives $\psi_1(z_+^{-r})+r=\psi(z)+r$, while on the $V_m^{-r}$ side it gives $\psi_0(z_-^0)-r=\psi(z)-r$. These are unequal unless $r=0$. Hence $\tilde\psi$ is not a well-defined function on the vertex set of $\Gamma_m$, and the symmetry argument for uniqueness of the minimizer fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a correct proof of harmonicity at the glued vertex, e.g., by directly verifying the discrete Laplace equation at $z$ using the jump condition and the minimization properties, without the ill-defined sheet-swapping symmetry.
issues.overall_effect: The proof that $\mathbf{f}^\ast$ is harmonic on the covering space (Theorem lem.ext_harmonic_on_G) is invalid, which undermines the harmonicity step in the construction of the main harmonic map.
issues.title: Ill-defined symmetry transformation in proof of lem.ext_harmonic_on_G
issues.why_classification: The lemma is central to the construction, but the statement is likely true and a contained direct verification can repair the proof.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with $w$ taken in  lexicographical order, i.e., $\gamma_0=\partial T_\emptyset, \gamma_1=\partial T_{1}, \gamma_2=\partial T_{2}, $ etc.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines the loops $\gamma_i$ in lexicographical order. For $w=12$, the lexicographical index is $5$ (after $11$), but the formula gives $\ell(12)=1+2\cdot3=7$. Thus $\rho_{\ell(w)}$ does not correspond to the winding number of $\partial T_w$. The higher-order covering space construction would use the wrong winding number for each cell.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the formula for $\ell(w)$ to match the lexicographical indexing, e.g., $\ell(w)=\sum_{m=0}^{|w|-1}3^m+\sum_{i=1}^{|w|}(w_i-1)3^{|w|-i}$.
issues.overall_effect: The construction for higher-order harmonic maps uses incorrect winding numbers, so the proof of Theorem thm.main for arbitrary degree vectors is invalid.
issues.title: Indexing formula for higher-order degree vector is inconsistent with lexicographical order
issues.why_classification: The error is a local indexing formula; correcting it is straightforward and preserves the higher-order construction.

issues.failure_explanation: For $w=\emptyset$, \eqref{eq:sg_gen_cuts} gives $v^k_{1\bar{3}}\simeq v^{k+\rho_0}_{3\bar{1}}$, whereas the correct identification from Section 4 is $v^k_{3\bar{1}}\simeq v^{k+\rho_0}_{1\bar{3}}$. The shift is applied to the opposite copy. This reverses the sign of the jump condition, producing degree $-\rho_0$ instead of $\rho_0$ for the outer loop, and the same error propagates to all higher cuts.

issues.title: Sign error in higher-order cut identifications
issues.why_classification: The error is a local sign correction in the identification formula; the construction can be repaired without new machinery.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\gamma_0\in\operatorname{Cyc}(\Gamma_m)$ be a cycle that contains boundary vertices $V_0\subset V(\gamma_0)$.
$K$ is called a p.c.f. fractal if $V_0$ is finite.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated for any p.c.f. fractal $K$, but the proof and the boundary condition \eqref{pcf-bc-hm} require a cycle $\gamma_0$ in $\operatorname{Cyc}(\Gamma_m)$ containing all boundary vertices $V_0$. This is not guaranteed for all p.c.f. fractals. For example, the unit interval with the standard two-map IFS is a p.c.f. fractal with $V_0=\{0,1\}$, but its approximating graphs are paths with no cycles, so no such $\gamma_0$ exists. The boundary value problem is therefore not well-defined for such $K$.

failure_location.quote: There is a HM $f\colon K\to\mathbb{T}$ satisfying \eqref{eq:winding_vec_general} and \eqref{pcf-bc-hm}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that there exists a cycle $\gamma_0\in\operatorname{Cyc}(\Gamma_m)$ containing $V_0$, or restrict the theorem to the class of p.c.f. fractals satisfying this condition.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm.pcf is not valid as stated for all p.c.f. fractals; its advertised scope must be restricted to those admitting such a boundary cycle.
issues.title: Missing hypothesis that a boundary cycle exists in thm.pcf
issues.why_classification: The missing hypothesis excludes a class of p.c.f. fractals (e.g., the interval) and changes the advertised scope of the extension to general p.c.f. fractals; the theorem is ill-posed for them.
